key_insight: Ta₃GeTe₆ hosts topological hourglass bands and spin-polarized surface states, with surface inversion-symmetry breaking implicated in nonreciprocal transport.
engineering_relevance: Its direction-dependent resistance could inform anisotropic electronic and spintronic devices, though device performance is not established.
method: ARPES and Hall/magnetotransport measurements probe electronic bands and transport.
Raman spectroscopy characterizes anisotropic phonon symmetries.
DFT and a phenomenological toy model connect surface spin splitting with nonreciprocal resistance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ARPES-observed hourglass and Rashba-type bands, direction-dependent magnetoresistance, and supporting DFT and toy-model results, without quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: The surface-state contribution to nonreciprocal transport needs quantitative isolation from bulk conduction before device-level claims can be assessed.
paper_title: Non-trivial topological spin-polarized surface states induced nonreciprocal transport in the hourglass semimetal
